about: Checks on the candidates our models proposed: measurements and calculations that someone has already done, hits and misses alike. A candidate stays on the list with its check attached, so that a wrong prediction is visible next to the prediction. This is the opposite of data/prior_claims.json, which holds superconductors reported by others and takes a material off the list altogether. A "formula" matches a material with the same elements and every share within 2 at.%. Each entry says only what its source says: where a paper reports a measurement but never uses the words "not superconducting", the note says what was measured and that no transition is reported.

asaba2024.cite: T. Asaba et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 3861 (2024)
asaba2024.quote: In this configuration, YbCoIn5 and YbRhIn5 act as conventional non-superconducting metals

shimozawa2012.cite: M. Shimozawa et al., Phys. Rev. B 86, 144526 (2012)
shimozawa2012.quote: YbCoIn5 is a conventional nonmagnetic metal with no superconducting transition down to 20 mK

cho2008.cite: J. Y. Cho et al., Chem. Mater. 20, 6116 (2008)

karaki1996.cite: Y. Karaki et al., Czech. J. Phys. 46, 2209 (1996)
karaki1996.quote: has been measured in the temperature range between 0.07 mK and 10 mK

materials.note: Grown as single crystals and used as the non-superconducting layers of a CeCoIn5 superlattice, which is the strongest statement an experiment can make about it: the paper calls YbRhIn5 a conventional non-superconducting metal. Ytterbium is divalent here, so the compound has none of the local moments that CeRhIn5 superconducts with.

The same superlattice work calls YbCoIn5 a conventional non-superconducting metal; no superconducting transition down to 20 mK has been reported (Phys. Rev. B 86, 144526 (2012), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.86.144526).

Single crystals measured by susceptibility, resistivity and specific heat from 0.35 K: a sharp specific-heat peak near 1.8 K marks antiferromagnetic order, and no superconducting transition is reported in that range.
The same work: antiferromagnetic order at 10 K, specific heat measured from 0.35 K, and no superconducting transition reported in that range.

Specific heat measured from 0.07 mK to 10 mK, with a nuclear magnetic ordering anomaly at 0.13 mK and no superconducting transition reported; PrIn3 is a van Vleck paramagnet with a non-magnetic crystal-field ground state.
